documents.title: Probiotics and diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania: secondary analysis of a randomised clinical trial.
documents.abstract: Diarrhoea causes annually more than 444 000 deaths in children globally, the majority in infants in low-income countries. The gut microbiota is a key determinant in resilience against enteric infections. We evaluated the effects of Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation on diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania and explored associations between the gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age and later diarrhoeal risk.

documents.title: CAnDi: a global catalogue of anaerobic digestion microbiomes.
documents.abstract: Methanogenic environments harbour complex prokaryotic consortia that drive the anaerobic conversion of organic matter into methane and carbon dioxide. Beyond being key to the global carbon cycle, such processes have been steered into powerful biotechnologies for energy production in bioreactors. Decoding the functional and taxonomic landscape of these communities requires comprehensive surveys, including bacteriophages and plasmids, which, however, remain vastly underrepresented in current databases. Here, we present the microbial Catalogue of Anaerobic Digestion (CAnDi), a database comprising

documents.title: Influence of Gliricidia sepium living support on rhizosphere bacterial recruitment and fruit metabolomics in black pepper (Piper nigrum).
documents.abstract: The ability of the rhizosphere to recruit beneficial microorganisms is central to the sustainable management of crops. Here, we investigated, through shotgun metagenomic sequencing and mass spectrometry techniques, the microbial composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMRs), and metabolomic profiles of Piper nigrum cultivated under two support systems: living Gliricidia sepium support (SL/RL) and dead wooden support (SD/RD). Bulk and rhizosphere soils were sequenced to assess taxonomic structure and ARGs, with emphasis on Actinobacteria due to their relevance in antibiotic production. Actinobac

documents.title: Assembly of minimally fragmented metagenomic pangenome graphs.
documents.abstract: Pangenome variation graphs are a powerful tool for representing genetic diversity within and across populations. For comparative and evolutionary genomic analyses leveraging these graph-based structures, it is important that graph topology reflects the underlying phylogenetic and genetic similarities of the genomes embedded within the graph. However, in metagenomic settings these approaches often produce highly fragmented multi-component graphs, hindering comparisons of genomes embedded across different components. This challenge is particularly pronounced for hypervariable viral families like
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Network perturbation of lactate metabolism identifies an aggressive hepatocellular carcinoma subtype with distinct immune and microbial features.
documents.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits significant heterogeneity, and the reprogramming of lactate metabolism (LM) plays a crucial role in tumor progression and immune evasion. Classification based on perturbations in the gene interaction network related to LM may reveal new molecular subtypes. This study aimed to construct an LM interaction perturbation-based classification of HCC and to characterize the clinical, immune, and intratumoral microbial features of the identified subtypes.

documents.title: Senimuribacter muris sp. nov., a butyrate-producing bacterium isolated from mouse feces, and reclassification of members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae.
documents.abstract: Two strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile, and rod-shaped bacterial strains, designated rT4E-8T and mB4P-1, were isolated from the feces of specific-pathogen-free Mus musculus (C57BL/6J). Both strains were catalase- and oxidase-negative and produced butyrate as a major fermentation product, with optimal growth at 37 °C and pH 7. The two strains shared 100% pairwise 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity and showed high similarity to Senimuribacter intestinalis DSM 106208T (95.1-95.3%). Genome sizes of strains rT4E-8T and mB4P-1 were 2.9 Mbp and 2.8 Mbp, with genomic DNA G+C contents o

documents.title: Taxonova: Deep learning enables fast and confidence-aware microbiome species-level amplicon classification.
documents.abstract: Accurate species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences remains challenging due to the difficulty of resolving subtle variations within conserved ribosomal regions. Traditional similarity-based methods struggle with short amplicons and sequences with poor database representation. No existing method performs robustly across the full spectrum of amplicon lengths, limiting applicability across diverse sequencing platforms and variable-region targets. We present Taxonova, a deep learning framework for both short- and long-read ribosomal amplicons. Evaluated across physical

documents.title: Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.
documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in microbiome research, yet the way microbiome scientists are trained has not kept pace. Existing discussions frequently emphasize AI literacy and responsible tool use. We argue that literacy alone is insufficient in a field where data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, inappropriate model selection and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. We propose an AI-competence framework comprising five connected capabilities: data and platform fluency, machine-learning comp

documents.title: Microencapsulated immunoglobulin Y and lactic acid bacteria improve intestinal health in Yanbian Yellow calves.
documents.abstract: Neonatal calf diarrhea remains a major cause of morbidity and growth impairment, highlighting the need for stable and effective antibiotic alternatives that can simultaneously suppress enteric pathogens and improve gut health. We aimed to develop microcapsules containing immunoglobulin Y (IgY) and mixed lactic acid bacteria (LAB), termed IgY-LAB-MCs, and to evaluate their efficacy and optimal dosage as an alternative strategy for preventing calf diarrhea.

documents.title: An integrated in vitro gastrointestinal digestion and fermentation model as a complementary tool for evaluating feed ingredients in young broilers: a case study with peas.
documents.abstract: The search for sustainable protein sources in broiler nutrition has increased interest in locally produced ingredients such as peas. However, nutritional evaluation of alternative feed ingredients relies on costly and ethically constrained animal trials, while standardized in vitro models representing the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers are lacking. These models should reflect their lower digestive capacity and less complex caecal microbiota. This study developed an innovative in vitro model simulating the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers and used peas as a c

documents.title: Advances in 16S Taxonomic Classification: Impacts on Species-Level Resolution of Female Bladder Microbiota.
documents.abstract: Bacteria are present in the human urinary bladder, even in the absence of infection. These bacteria comprise the urinary microbiome, or urobiome, and have the potential to promote bladder health or contribute to pathology. Despite its importance, studying the urobiome remains challenging given the high proportion of host to bacterial cells and low microbial biomass. The leading method for studying the urobiome has been 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. This culture-independent approach provides a cost-effective method for identifying bacteria, but taxonomic classification accuracy depends on three
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Multikingdom and functional gut microbiota markers for cholangiocarcinoma.
documents.abstract: While the association between gut microbiota and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) has been explored, existing research has been limited to bacterial components. The alterations in non-bacterial members (fungi, archaea, and viruses) and their functional characteristics in CCA remain unclear. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the multi-kingdom gut microbiota and functional profiles in CCA patients and develop a non-invasive diagnostic model.

documents.title: Shifts in the Maternal Gut Microbiome Across Pregnancy are Associated with Energetic Status in Phayre's Leaf Monkeys.
documents.abstract: During pregnancy, mothers experience physiological changes that support fetal development, including shifts in energy utilization and increasing insulin resistance during late gestation. While these changes benefit the fetus, they can also impose energetic costs that affect the mother's physical condition and metabolic phenotype. Previous studies suggest that the gut microbiome, a key regulator of female metabolism and energy harvest, may play a critical role in mediating these physiological challenges.
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Disrupted microbial queuosine biosynthesis contributes to dysbiosis in human inflammatory bowel disease.
documents.abstract: As a microbiome/diet-derived vitamin, queuine (q) is a micronutrient that eukaryotes acquire from microbiota or diet. Vitamin q, the free base form of queuosine (Q), is used for Q-modification of transfer RNA (tRNA). Although tRNA-Q-modification in regulating eukaryotic cell physiology is recognized, the relationship between Q-tRNA-modification and the human microbiome in health and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) remains unknown. Which bacteria produce q and how the q-producing bacteria contributing to human health and IBD are not explored. Here, we hypothesize that disrupted microbial Q-bi
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Elevated Level of Fannyhessea vaginae Correlated with Implantation Outcomes in Women undergoing in vitro fertilization Treatment.
documents.abstract: The vaginal microbiome plays a significant role in reproductive health. While maintaining a balanced vaginal microbiome is crucial for successful in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, the specific bacteria associated with adverse outcomes may vary by region and are largely unknown. This study aims to investigate the bacterial profiles and their influence on embryo implantation, thereby supporting the development of microbiome-based therapies. One hundred women undergoing IVF provided vaginal swabs at three stages: oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and hCG pregnancy testing. An in-house 16S r

documents.title: Temperature effects on life history strategies for rapid growth potential of leaf epiphytic bacteria.
documents.abstract: Phyllosphere bacteria, occupying both epiphytic and endophytic habitats, constitute a critical plant-atmosphere interface. However, their community assembly and life-history strategies (LHSs) in response to temperature increase remain poorly understood. Here, we compared leaf phyllosphere bacterial communities with those in other plant compartments across four representative plant species from an alpine meadow on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. By combining observations along an elevational gradient with a controlled warming experiment, we found that temperature was closely associated with the dete

documents.title: Identification of ebastine and ceritinib as effective inhibitors of Fusobacterium nucleatum FtsZ.
documents.abstract: The role of microorganisms in cancer is not a new concept-bacteria, parasites, and viruses have all been implicated in cancer development. Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of the oral microbiota, has emerged as an important cancer-associated bacterium. Unbiased global genomic analyses have demonstrated that F. nucleatum is enriched in human colorectal cancer (CRC) tissues compared with noncancerous colorectal tissues, underscoring the urgent need for specific antimicrobial agents targeting F. nucleatum for CRC prevention and treatment. In this study, structure-based virtual screening successf

documents.title: Children at risk of vitamin A deficiency exhibit taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome: a matched case-control study.
documents.abstract: Vitamin A deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies worldwide. This condition increases susceptibility to infections and due to its role in intestinal barrier integrity, it has been suggested that it could predispose to gut dysbiosis.

documents.title: Sex influences the mosquito virome in a host-specific way.
documents.abstract: Mosquitoes harbor diverse eukaryotic viruses. These viral communities, or viromes, probably influence mosquito physiology, including pathogen transmission. However, the factors shaping the virome remain largely unstudied, limiting our understanding of its role in mosquito biology. Here, we assess the influence of sex on the eukaryotic virome of mosquitoes. Ecological differences between males and females, such as female-specific blood feeding, may lead to differential viral exposure and virome structure. We investigated the influence of sex in sympatric populations of Culex quinquefasciatus an

documents.title: Diversity and evolution of the ribovirian class Stelpaviricetes.
documents.abstract: Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized virus families: order Stellavirales with family Astroviridae infecting vertebrates; Patatavirales with families Potyviridae, the largest known family of plant ribovirians, and Potyliviridae; and Hypofuvirales consisting of three families of viruses associated largely with phytopathogenic fungi. Using an order-specific collection of Hidden Markov Model profiles for t

documents.title: Physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape interactions in the plant growth-promoting maize rhizosphere synthetic community.
documents.abstract: Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. Here we describe the maize rhizosphere synthetic community (MARSc), a genome-enabled 31-member bacterial community representative of the diversity found on the roots of maize grown in Iowa soils. This community is bui

documents.title: Exploring normality: Mapping the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Argentina.
documents.abstract: The human microbiome varies according to individual and geographic characteristics. The endometrial microbiome plays a relevant role in reproductive physiology; however, data from healthy South American populations remain scarce. This prospective observational study aimed to characterize the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Rosario, Argentina and to establish a regional baseline for future research. A total of 100 healthy women aged 22-50 years from Rosario, Argentina, were included. Endometrial samples were obtained by aspiration biopsy during the follicular phas

documents.title: Monitoring single-cell metabolic phenotyping changes of Daqu microbiota during fermentation by Raman spectroscopy.
documents.abstract: Monitoring microbial community dynamics during natural food fermentation is essential for stabilizing fermentation processes and improving product flavor profiles. This study employed single-cell Raman spectroscopy to monitor the metabolic change of Daqu microbiota during fermentation. First, we developed an operational phenotypic unit (OPU)-based clustering method to process Raman spectral data of a nine-member microbial community. The clustering was validated by sorting out representative single cells from different OPUs and performing 16S/ITS region sequencing. Second, single-cell Raman spe

documents.title: Scaffold-level validation is needed for phage-host inference from metagenome-assembled genomes.
documents.abstract: Accurate phage-host prediction underpins ecological interpretation and experimental validation of uncultivated phages, yet most current approaches rely heavily on metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). This reliance implicitly assumes that MAG-level quality metrics, such as completeness and contamination, ensure scaffold-level correctness. Here, we demonstrate that this assumption can be violated under particular challenging conditions. Tetranucleotide frequency (TNF) analyses reveal that CRISPR-associated regions often diverge compositionally from their host genomes, increasing the risk of misb

documents.title: Optimized Super-SILAC Normalization Enables Enhanced Profiling of Histone Post-Translational Modification Changes Associated with Microbiota and Acute Inflammation.
documents.abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that modulate histone acylation and serve as precursors for non-acetyl acyl marks, representing a mechanism in host-microbiome epigenetic crosstalk. However, the reliable quantification of these low-abundance modifications in complex tissues remains challenging. Here, we established an optimized, non-acetyl histone acylation-focused super-SILAC strategy for profiling histone post-translational modifications (HPTM) in the gut epithelium. We generated a functionally optimized internal standard from heavy-labeled col

documents.title: Shotgun metagenomic characterization of human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in pediatric prolonged diarrhea: a genome-resolved case study.
documents.abstract: Viral and bacterial pathogens may be concurrently detected in pediatric gastroenteritis, yet such findings are often missed by routine diagnostic methods. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing enables comprehensive detection and genomic characterization of microorganisms present in clinical specimens, including pathogens that may not be recovered by conventional testing.

documents.title: Genome-resolved taxonomy, global distribution, and EPS potential of Zoogloea, the canonical floc-former in wastewater treatment systems.
documents.abstract: The bacterial genus Zoogloea is the fourth most abundant genus in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) globally, where it plays key roles in floc formation and nutrient removal but can also contribute to viscous bulking when highly abundant. The taxonomic assignment of Zoogloea has historically been inconsistent, as several taxa were classified based on phenotypic characteristics and later reassigned to other families or orders. This has obscured both the identity and distribution of Zoogloea and hindered interpretation of its floc-forming mechanisms, which have been attributed to polysaccharid

documents.title: Reciprocity between the intestinal microbiome and urobiome in children with and without urinary tract infection: protocol of a single-centre, nested case-control study in Denmark.
Global Carriage of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Virulence Factors Among Physicians in Cirrhosis Care.
documents.abstract: Cirrhosis patients are at high risk for drug-resistant infections, which may be transmitted between patients and healthcare providers. In this study, we used shotgun metagenomics to characterize the fecal microbiome of physicians in cirrhosis care (n = 55) across 9 countries. Our results indicate physicians from low- or middle-income countries carry greater antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) diversity corresponding to increased taxonomic richness. Physicians carried a low prevalence of clinically relevant ARGs or virulence factors (VFs), regardless of country of practice or patient exposure.

documents.title: Importance of rumen ciliated protozoa and current research techniques for their analysis.
documents.abstract: Rumen protozoa are an integral component of the ruminant foregut microbiome, with a profound influence on feed digestion, microbial ecosystem dynamics and enteric methane emissions. Although they represent only a small proportion of species richness, protozoa contribute significantly to microbial biomass and functions in fibre degradation, volatile fatty acid production, microbial protein turnover, pH modulation and hydrogen-mediated methanogenesis. In addition to highlighting their importance to rumen function, this review summarizes classical and contemporary methodologies for enumerating, i

documents.title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel Gemella species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
documents.abstract: Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.

documents.title: Benchmarking nanopore-based strategies for antimicrobial resistance prediction.
documents.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents a pressing need to ensure that the right antimicrobials are used to target the right microbes at the right time. Ideally, the appropriate antimicrobial is selected after patient samples have been cultured and assessed with antimicrobial sensitivity testing (AST). However, the time needed for culture-based diagnosis leads to immediate empirical treatment, often with broad-spectrum and/or high-tier antimicrobials. Direct nanopore metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to identify pathogens and predict their AMR is a rapid and patient-side alternative. A limit

documents.title: Seasonal and Environmental Influences on Microbial Community Dynamics in the Dunk River Watershed, Prince Edward Island, Canada.
documents.abstract: Riverine ecosystems are crucial biogeochemical hubs, with their microbial communities playing a key role in nutrient cycling and overall ecosystem health. This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize the seasonal and environmental drivers of taxonomic and functional microbial community structure (read depth between 1.91 and 30.44 bp) in four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island (PEI), a landscape shaped by intensive agriculture and groundwater-dominated streamflow, where the seasonal and land-use impacts on the river's microbiome remain understudied

documents.title: Planetary-scale metagenomic analysis reveals CRISPR targeting dynamics across ecosystems.
documents.abstract: Interactions between microorganisms and their mobile genetic elements (MGEs), including viruses and plasmids, impact microbiome dynamics. CRISPR-Cas systems are important regulators of these host-MGE interactions, but a global understanding of the diversity, activity and roles of CRISPR spacers across Earth's biomes is still lacking. Here we develop a computational approach to search short-read data and collect 794 million CRISPR spacers across 367,609 public metagenomes, from which we identified 1.18 billion hits between 41 million spacers and 2.5 million viruses and plasmids. While spacers w

documents.title: Cross hybridization inference for phylogenetic resolution-fluorescence in situ hybridization enables microbiome imaging with strain level taxonomic resolution.
documents.abstract: The spatial organization of microbial communities is a critical determinant of host-microbe interactions, yet species-level mapping remains challenging due to high 16S rRNA sequence homology and spectral crosstalk in multiplexed fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). To address this challenge, we developed Cross-hybridization Inference for Phylogenetic Resolution (CIPHR)-FISH, a pipeline that integrates strategic probe design with supervised machine learning. CIPHR-FISH transforms probe cross-hybridization, traditionally viewed as experimental noise, into informative molecular signatures.

documents.title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
documents.abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustme

documents.title: Human milk oligosaccharides are distinctly processed by early life gut microbial sialidases.
documents.abstract: The infant gut microbiome in early life is shaped by numerous factors, including feeding method. Exclusively breastfed and formula-fed infants exhibit distinct microbiome compositions. While these effects are well-established, the underlying mechanisms that drive these differences are not fully understood. Here, we examine the removal of sialic acid from human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) influenced by human microbial sialidases in early life. We identify 351 and 214 unique sialidase sequences from adult and infant microbiome metagenomes, respectively, and characterize a diverse, representativ

documents.title: Metagenomic characterization of gut microbiota in patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction.
documents.abstract: Patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI) experience recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms without identifiable organic abnormalities. While earlier studies focused on neural and hormonal regulation, recent evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolism may play key roles in DGBI.

documents.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils.
documents.abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified ph

documents.title: A systematic review of the effects of diet on the gut microbiota in individuals at elevated risk for colorectal cancer.
documents.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) poses a major public health concern, with emerging evidence highlighting the critical role of the gut microbiota in CRC progression. Considering that diet is a major modifiable factor influencing CRC risk, partly through its interaction with the gut microbiome, this systematic review evaluated the effects of dietary intervention RCTs, including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns, on the gut microbiome in elevated-risk individuals.

documents.title: Co-occurrence and genetic contexts of NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1 carbapenemase genes in a critically ill patient.
documents.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant organisms are increasingly reported in clinical settings, yet the simultaneous detection of multiple carbapenemase genes within a single specimen remains rare.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

documents.title: Why does apical periodontitis persist? A shotgun metagenomic survey of the microbial community in primary and persistent periapical granulomas.
documents.abstract: This cross‑sectional observational study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbiomes of periapical granulomas from primary and persistent apical periodontitis to identify microbial taxa and functional pathways associated with persistent lesions.

documents.title: A Two-Stage ESM-Based Machine Learning Pipeline for Robust Hierarchically Evaluated Enzyme Function Prediction.
documents.abstract: Accurate enzyme annotation remains a major bottleneck in translating rapidly growing protein sequence data into biological knowledge. Enzyme Commission (EC) prediction is particularly challenging because enzyme functions are organized hierarchically, annotations are often imbalanced across classes, and sequence similarity alone may be insufficient to resolve functional differences. To address these challenges, we developed ESM-ECForest, a 2-stage framework that combines protein embeddings generated by the pretrained language model ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2) with random forest classi

documents.title: Microbiome-driven precision psychiatry: integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and personalized interventions along the gut-brain axis.
documents.abstract: This scoping review maps evidence for microbiome-driven precision psychiatry in depression and anxiety.

documents.title: Gut mycobiome dysbiosis in inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
documents.abstract: The intestinal mycobiome is increasingly recognized as an important component of host-microbiota interactions in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet its contribution to intestinal immune dysregulation remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize alterations in the intestinal mycobiome in patients with inflammatory bowel disease, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, compared with individuals without IBD, focusing on fungal diversity, taxonomic composition, and relative abundance, as well as their potential associations with disease phenotype and inflammatory activ

documents.title: Changes in the Gut Microbiota Composition and Metabolic Pathways in Six-Week-Old HIV Exposed Breastfed Infants Receiving Antiretroviral Prophylaxis.
documents.abstract: Understanding the association of HIV exposure, antiretroviral therapy (ART) prophylaxis and human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) on the gut microbiota of breastfed infants is crucial for developing strategies to promote infant health. Our study explored gut microbiota diversity and development in breastfed infants, analysing the influence of nevirapine (NVP) in HIV Exposed infants and HMOs in HIV Unexposed infants.

documents.title: Edible insect-based feed ingredients as modulators of gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species.
documents.abstract: Edible insects have emerged as promising sustainable feed ingredients capable of supporting both animal production and gastrointestinal health. Beyond their nutritional value, insect-derived meals contain bioactive compounds-including chitin, antimicrobial peptides, medium-chain fatty acids, micronutrients, and antioxidant molecules-that may modulate gut microbiota-host interactions in farmed monogastric animal species. This review critically examines current evidence on the mechanisms through which insect-based diets influence gastrointestinal physiology in livestock and aquaculture species.

documents.title: Clear aligner interface properties, oral microbial ecology, and strategies for biofilm control and caries-risk mitigation: a scoping review.
documents.abstract: Clear aligners create an aligner-tooth interface that may retain saliva, microorganisms, and dietary substrates. Evidence linking interface properties, oral microecological responses, and preventive interventions remains fragmented.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

documents.title: Characterization of lower-airway microbial communities in pulmonary tuberculosis by BALF metagenomic sequencing.
documents.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) is an infectious disease caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC). This study aimed to characterize the lower-airway microbiome in patients with PTB and compare it with that of patients without PTB (Non-PTB) undergoing bronchoscopy for pulmonary disease, in order to describe differences in microbial composition between the two groups and improve our understanding of pulmonary microbial ecology in tuberculosis.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

documents.title: Decoding pyroptosis at single-cell resolution: heterogeneity, microenvironment remodeling and potential translational insights.
documents.abstract: Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory programmed cell death mediated by inflammatory caspases and Gasdermin (GSDM) family proteins, exerts dual roles in host defense and pathological damage. Traditional bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) is limited in capturing single-cell heterogeneity and dissecting intercellular communication, impeding in-depth mechanistic exploration of pyroptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these limitations, enabling high-throughput profiling of single-cell transcriptomes and precise characterization of gene expression heter

documents.title: Harnessing metatranscriptomics to unveil the metabolic landscape of microbiota in traditional fermented foods.
documents.abstract: Traditional fermented foods are widely consumed and valued for their distinctive sensory properties and potential health benefits. These foods contain complex microbiota whose interactions and metabolic activities shape biochemical transformations relevant to product quality, safety, and functionality. Metatranscriptomics provides a culture-independent means of profiling community RNA and examining changes in microbial gene expression during fermentation. However, most fermented-food microbiome studies continue to infer function from community composition or genomic potential rather than from

documents.title: Dietary exogenous microRNAs in the gut: biological effects, mechanistic evidence, and controversies.
documents.abstract: Dietary exogenous microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as potential mediators of interorganismal communication, with growing interest in their ability to influence gastrointestinal physiology and the gut microbiota. These molecules encompass plant-derived miRNAs implicated in cross-kingdom regulation, animal-derived dietary miRNAs involved in cross-species communication, and maternal milk miRNAs that may participate in mother-to-offspring molecular crosstalk. A proportion of dietary miRNAs are associated with extracellular vesicles or other protective complexes, which may enhance their stability du

documents.title: Building biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota: methodological considerations, current challenges, and future perspectives.
documents.abstract: The human gut microbiota (HGM) plays a pivotal role in human health by regulating metabolic, immune, and neurological processes and contributes to the susceptibility to various diseases. The increasing interest in microbiota-targeted therapies has highlighted the need for in vitro models capable of accurately reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem. This review examines the methodological factors that determine the biological relevance of HGM in vitro models, emphasizing that reliable experimental outcomes depend not only on the choi

documents.title: Interpretable detection-based image classification for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using smartphone-assisted microscopy.
documents.abstract: The vaginal discharge is a common clinical presentation associated with diverse infectious and microbiota-related conditions. Existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic approaches have predominantly focused on detection of individual pathogens and have rarely integrated microbiota-associated conditions within a diagnostic framework. We developed an explainable deep learning framework for automated analysis of Gram-stained vaginal smear images acquired using handheld smartphones or tablets positioned over a conventional light microscope eyepiece.
